edits.old_text: The landing page serves as the primary system entry and initial access gateway of the TeleConsole web application (/). Designed with a clean, minimalist interface, the screen presents the platform title accompanied by the subtitle "Secure video consultation platform." To enforce clear role-based segmentation upon entry, the interface is bifurcated into two distinct operational cards: the For Doctors module, which directs clinical practitioners toward administrative authentication for room creation, invitation management, and clinical history review via a primary blue action button (Sign in as Doctor), and the For Patients module, which routes end-users toward consultation access via a green action button (Sign in as Patient).
edits.replacement: The landing page introduces TeleConsole and its doctor and patient entry paths. Doctors use /doctor/login for invitations, admission and their clinical records; patients use /patient/login or a valid invitation. Clinic administrators use /admin/login and platform owners /super-admin/login. These later staff entry routes share Firebase identity, not clinical authority: the server resolves permission and scope, and rejects the wrong audience. Both administrator levels use /admin for staff provisioning; an audit/metrics oversight dashboard is proposed. The historical screenshot is not evidence that respondents evaluated these later changes. Scheduling stays hidden until its default-off server capability passes the documented release gates.
edits.reason: Correct administrative-versus-clinical entry wording and distinguish later role routes, future oversight and gated scheduling from the historical screenshot.
